routes.description: The iconic reef crossing: Marco Zero plaza to the Brennand sculpture park on the harbor breakwater. Operates today in small open outboard boats at R$5 round trip, daylight only (haversine 0.18 nm pier-to-pier). The shortest, most-loved hop in the mesh and the natural first electric conversion.

The Venice-of-Brazil bridges run: Recife Antigo waterfront to the Cais de Santa Rita quay through the Capibaribe bridge canyon (Ponte Maurício de Nassau, Ponte Buarque de Macedo). Haversine 0.45 nm; set to ~1.0 nm because the water path wraps around the tip of the Recife Antigo/Santo Antônio islands rather than cutting across land. Corridor plied daily by Catamaran Tours' R$90-95 sightseeing circuits.

Marco Zero to the Rua da Aurora pastel waterfront up the Capibaribe's north arm, passing under Ponte do Limoeiro. Haversine 0.58 nm; set to ~0.9 nm for the river wrap around the north tip of Recife Antigo island. Existing tour catamarans transit this arm; as transport it links the historic core to Boa Vista/Santo Amaro.

Cruise-day shuttle: the Porto do Recife passenger terminal (19 calls / 30,000+ pax in 2024/25) to Marco Zero along the inner harbor quay (haversine 0.39 nm). No water service exists today — cruise guests currently walk or bus. First leg of a cruise-day water circuit feeding the whole mesh.

Cais de Santa Rita to Cabanga Iate Clube across the Pina basin (haversine 1.06 nm, mostly open sheltered water; small margin for the marked channel). Connects the new Recife Marina complex to the city's flagship yacht club — the two already partner on nautical tourism.

Basin run between Recife's two Refeno-partner yacht clubs, Cabanga and the Pernambuco Iate Clube (former Casa de Banhos) inside the Dique do Recife (haversine 1.2 nm across the sheltered Pina basin, small channel margin).

Pina basin to Marco Zero through the inner-harbor channel (haversine 0.42 nm; set to ~0.7 nm as the water path follows the dique and port channel around the São José shore). Ties the yacht-club cluster into the historic-core mesh.
Short spur along the Dique do Recife linking Iate Clube do Recife (Brasília Teimosa) to the PIC (haversine 0.61 nm inside the sheltered basin, small margin for the dique channel).

The river commute Recife already planned: up the Capibaribe from the Rua da Aurora pier toward Derby, the first-phase station of the shelved Rios da Gente west corridor (documented corridor: 11 km / ~5.9 nm, Estação Central metro ↔ Iputinga/BR-101 via Derby, Torre and Santana; designed for 300,000 pax/month — a projection never validated). Distance left null: the Derby station site has no verifiable public coordinate, so no haversine is computed. Shallow-draft N35 suits the silted upper river; the state's partial 2013 dredging is a reusable asset.
